findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: register) — B is self-defeating: a drop weight released “from whatever height each point seemed to need” cannot yield the comparable counts the set elsewhere reports, so one option falls on coherence alone. A single weak distractor is ordinary design, not a channel.

CROSS_QUESTION (assessed, non-operative) — the set is internally inconsistent about the instrument (A describes a cone pushed through, B and C a dropped weight with a blow count), which lets a blind reader infer the device is a drop hammer; it narrows nothing further.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: odd-one-out, non-operative) — D is formally mismatched to the stem (“his work in the school”, singular) because it compares one arena with the next; a mild tilt, not an elimination.
justification: Blind pick C at roughly 40 percent, only marginally above the 25 percent base rate. B eliminates on incoherence, leaving a three-way residual near base rate; per the binding calibration that residual is inert and is not scored. No option is handed to a passage-blind reader. Clean.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION — Q5 option A presupposes the exact proposition Q2 option C asserts: “the part of the bed that the tines were leaving unturned”. A distractor in a sibling question supplies this question's key content as a given.
CROSS_QUESTION — tine/harrow depth is signposted three further times in Q5 (A, C and D), so the tine finding reads as the unit's salient result before the passage is opened.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: odd-one-out) — A, B and D are all material-degradation findings (wax worn, grains broken down, fibre migrated); C is the only structural finding and so reads as the substantive one.
justification: Blind pick C at roughly 55-58 percent, sitting on the flag/kill boundary. The dominant driver is the presupposition embedded in Q5-A, and it is student-available: a reader working the set in order holds the tine-depth fact before reaching Q2. Repair belongs in Q5-A (strip the presupposition), not in Q2.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE — B and C contradict directly on one variable (whether sprinkler-kept schools have wax on their sand). The “the key is usually one of the two that disagree” heuristic is standard HP prep and halves the field; student-available.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: absolutizers) — C carries the set's strongest unhedged claim, “stays the same whatever the room does”, which marks it as the losing member of the contradictory pair.

WORLD_KNOWLEDGE — waxed and watered are alternative arena binder systems, so C is category-confused for anyone who knows arena footing, and wax is the temperature-sensitive binder, not the stable one. Expert-only.
justification: Blind pick B at roughly 52 percent. The contradictory pair is a genuine student-available channel but it only halves the field: A is a live limitation-shaped key (the watered schools may simply be newer beds), and A gains rather than loses if Q4 keys the writer's praise for self-imposed limits. Flag, not kill.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: register/prestige) — A credits the subject with methodological candour, while C dismisses riders as expectancy and D credits trade brochures; neither is a position a careful essayist takes, so two options fall on stance alone.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: altitude) — B conflates a subsequent action with evidence (“what the yard has since done as an answer”), a recognisable fallacy shape that reads as manufactured.
justification: Blind pick A at roughly 55 percent. The epistemic-virtue asymmetry is real and student-available, but B remains a live key: an essayist can well read what the yard did next as its own kind of answer. Below the kill threshold.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: hedging) — a clean 2+2 split: A (“probably”) and D (“may”) hedged against B and C unhedged. Per the binding calibration a 2+2 pair IS a channel; HP conclusion keys are almost always hedged, so the field halves before any content is read.

CROSS_QUESTION — A's clause “the part of the bed that the tines were leaving unturned” sits badly with Q2-C's picture of that layer as loose and out of reach of the hoofprints above it, so a reader who takes Q2-C demotes A inside the hedged pair.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: altitude) — C is the “combine both named variables” option (temperature plus tine depth), the standard too-tidy distractor.
justification: Blind pick D at roughly 45-50 percent. The 2+2 hedging split is a binding channel and halves the set; the cross-question conflict then tilts the residual pair to D. Neither step alone clears 60 percent, but the hedging split is the repairable defect: modality should be 3+1 or 4+0 across the set, never 2+2.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: odd-one-out) — assessed and NOT operative: “Elsewhere” is the only spatial adverb among three logical connectives, but it is fully idiomatic as a topic-shift marker in this register and is not eliminable.
justification: Four distinct discourse relations (consequence, correction, addition, topic shift) with no formal tell and no length or register asymmetry. Blind pick B at roughly 30 percent, essentially base rate. Clean.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION (topic only) — the option sets of gaps 2 and 3 both draw on deal-making vocabulary, which reveals the passage's subject matter to a blind reader but leaks no gap's key.
justification: Four high-frequency monosyllabic verbs, each idiomatically productive in a different frame (join forces, cut a deal, fall somewhere between, break off). Blind pick C at roughly 30 percent, essentially base rate. Clean.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: odd-one-out) — a 3+1 exclusivity cluster (negotiation is the process; transaction, bargain and settlement are outcomes). Per the binding calibration a 3+1 cluster is INERT base rate and is NOT scored.
justification: Within the three outcome nouns there is no formal separator; only register (plain prose against legal/technical) gives a weak tilt to “bargain”. Blind pick C at roughly 30 percent. Clean.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: odd-one-out) — assessed and NOT operative: “rehearsed” and “wholehearted” sit on a sincerity axis while “outspoken” and “brief” sit on manner and length axes. This is a loose semantic grouping, not a 2+2 exclusivity split, so the binding 2+2 rule does not bite.
justification: No option is excluded by form and none is raised above base rate. Blind pick A at roughly 30 percent. Clean.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: odd-one-out) — a 3+1 cluster (“narrowly” is a degree/margin adverb, the other three are dispositional). Per the binding calibration this is INERT base rate and is NOT scored; being the outlier does not make an option wrong.
justification: Blind pick C at roughly 30 percent, essentially base rate. Clean.

findings: WORLD_KNOWLEDGE — clinical knowledge of pneumatic-tube haemolysis eliminates B (haemolysis is visible only in spun serum or plasma, never in a whole-blood tube on the ward) and casts doubt on C (many laboratories forbid tubing blood-gas samples for exactly this reason). EXPERT-ONLY: unavailable to an HP student.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: register) — D is the only mechanism claim in the set, and a quoted expert is the conventional source of the mechanism, which tilts the residual pair toward D.
justification: Blind pick D at roughly 50 percent. World knowledge does not separate A from D — slowing the loop and arrival-shock damage are both attested in the literature — so the channel narrows the field to two without deciding it. Flag; because the eliminating route is expert-only, the practical student-facing leak is smaller than the figure suggests.

findings: PAIR_STRUCTURE — A and D converge on the same reading (the railway is the real stake in the quarrel), which signposts the passage's point before it is read. C is the lone counter-reading and B the throwaway trivial cause.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: altitude) — the stem asks what is implied, and A attributes a specific tactical intention to a named attorney, which is too strong for an inference key; that leaves D as the modest factual coincidence, the canonical shape of an implied key.
justification: Blind pick D at roughly 55 percent, student-available: the convergence heuristic (two options pointing the same way name the theme) plus the implied-versus-asserted altitude test does most of the work. Below kill because C is a live key: the chronology reading, that the quarrel predates the surveyor, is exactly what a period piece implies.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: 2+2) — a double-encoded 2+2 split: A and B are the strong positions and share the identical “även om” concessive, while C and D are the cautious positions and use different subordinators (“i den takt som”, “innan”). Per the binding calibration a 2+2 pair IS a channel, and here the syntactic split coincides exactly with the stance split, so it halves the field twice over.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: register) — the stem asks for a skribent's inställning in what reads as a debattartikel, and a columnist takes a strong position; that is the same half the connective tic marks.
PAIR_STRUCTURE (assessed, not scored) — a 3+1 on the deontic “bör” (A, C and D prescribe; B characterises the opponent). Per the binding calibration the 3+1 cluster is INERT and is NOT scored.
justification: Blind pick B at roughly 40 percent. The 2+2 is a real channel and it is doubly signalled, but it does not separate A from B: A is a concrete policy demand and B a characterisation of the objection, and the stem is compatible with either. Flag; the connective tic should be broken so the stance split is not also a syntax split.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION (STRONG FORM) — the proposition “there is a small countable set of surtitled evenings” survives across three of the four Q1 options (explicit in C, “Antalet textade kvällar bör utökas”; presupposed by A and by D), and A is the only Q2 option that engages a count. A sibling question hands the blind reader this question's answer-shape. STUDENT-AVAILABLE.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: odd-one-out) — B, C and D are layout trivia while A is the quantity the argument turns on; C in particular (who runs the technology) is eliminable as argumentatively inert.

PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: altitude) — A is the only numeric option, so there is no number-swap set; a lone number in a detail item reads as either the key or a lone plant, and the Q1 leak resolves that ambiguity toward key.
justification: Blind pick A at roughly 52-55 percent. Below the kill threshold because D is a live key: a debattartikel would plausibly note that the row sits squeezed between the syntolkning and the skolföreställningar, the same rhetorical move at a different altitude. Flag; see the pair line for the full Rule 15 analysis.

findings: CROSS_QUESTION (STRONG FORM) — the proposition “horses and teams did the work” survives across three of the four Q2 options (A's “Hushållen turades om och delade på vändorna”, C and D), which eliminates Q1-C (“Hästarna ersattes av folk på skidor”) before the passage is read. STUDENT-AVAILABLE.
PAIR_STRUCTURE — B and D contradict on one variable (did the hooves cope on the ice, or slip on it), the standard “one of the two that disagree” shape.

TIC — three options open with “Hovarna” and one with “Hästarna”, a lexical 3+1 marking C as the outlier. Per the binding calibration the 3+1 is INERT on its own and is NOT scored, but it reinforces the semantic elimination above.
justification: Blind pick A at roughly 42 percent. One option is removed by the sibling question's leak; the residual three are not separable blind — A encodes a bearing crust, B a solved problem, D a generic slip. Flag.

findings: PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: register/stem-fit) — the stem asks how the work was “lades upp” and A is the only option that states an arrangement; B, C and D state timing, duration and routing. Exactly one option answers the question as asked. STUDENT-AVAILABLE.
WORLD_KNOWLEDGE — a household rota for winter road-breaking is the canonical Swedish arrangement, reinforcing A; semi-student-available in Sweden.

CROSS_QUESTION — Q1's surface-condition options (A, B and D all make the snow or ice the governing problem) leak toward B here (weather-driven, days undecidable in advance) and against D (same routes as the rest of the year), which pulls against the stem-fit signal.
PARTIALLY_ANSWERABLE (form: absolutizers) — C over-claims (“en enda lång natt”).
justification: Blind pick A at roughly 55 percent. Two channels point in different directions, which is precisely what holds this below the kill threshold: stem-fit nominates A while the Q1 leak nominates B. Flag; the repair is to make more than one option actually answer the “hur lades arbetet upp” question.

findings: ONE-WAY LEAK (Q1 -> Q2, STRONG FORM) — the proposition “there is a small, countable set of surtitled evenings” survives across three of four Q1 options: explicit in C (“Antalet textade kvällar bör utökas”), presupposed by A (“Allt på stora scenen bör textas” presupposes that not all currently is), presupposed by D (“provas ett spelår ... innan den sätts in på stora scenen”). Q2 offers exactly one option about a count (A, “Den rymmer åtta kvällar”). A sibling question therefore hands the blind reader Q2's answer-shape. Strong form satisfied.

ONE-WAY LEAK (Q2 -> Q1) — Q2 options A and D both presuppose an established surtitling row already printed in the season programme beside the syntolkning and the skolföreställningar; that eliminates Q1-D, which proposes trialling surtitling for a season before it reaches the main stage. Weaker than the forward leak: one option removed, no answer supplied.

STEM SUPPLY — yes, partly. Q2's own stem, “raden för textade föreställningar”, already asserts that surtitled performances occupy a single row in a programme table, i.e. a bounded set. The stem does part of the leaking on its own, so the repair cannot be confined to the options.

SYMMETRIC VOUCHING — yes, one small factual world. Q1 supplies the two stages, the ensemble, the caption strip and the contested count; Q2 supplies the brochure row, the spread, the technology and the neighbouring accessibility services. Jointly they reconstruct a county theatre with a main and a small stage, a season brochure carrying an accessibility block, an ensemble that resists the strip, and a live argument about expanding a small number of surtitled evenings. Each question's options confirm the other's world rather than testing it.
justification: Joint stems-only solvability is elevated but not decisive. Best blind pair Q1=B, Q2=A at about 0.40 x 0.53 = 21 percent joint, against a 6.25 percent independent base rate — a 3.4x lift. The forward leak is strong form (a proposition surviving three options) and is student-available, since both questions sit on the same page. It does not reach kill because neither question individually clears 60 percent. Repair: drop “Antalet” from Q1-C and recast it as a stance about the ensemble's pace rather than a count, or replace Q2-A so the count is not the only quantitative option; and reword the Q2 stem so it does not itself assert a bounded row.

findings: ONE-WAY LEAK (Q2 -> Q1, STRONG FORM) — the proposition “horses and teams did the work” survives across three of four Q2 options (A “Hushållen turades om och delade på vändorna”, C “under en enda lång natt”, D “samma vägar som resten av året”). It eliminates Q1-C, “Hästarna ersattes av folk på skidor”, without the passage. Strong form satisfied.

ONE-WAY LEAK (Q1 -> Q2, STRONG FORM) — the proposition “the winter surface state governed the work” survives across three of four Q1 options (A sinking through, B studs in the shoes, D slipping on the glaze). It favours Q2-B (the days could not be fixed in advance, i.e. weather-driven) and disfavours Q2-D (same routes as the rest of the year), since a bearing crust or a frozen route is exactly what changes the routes. Strong form satisfied in both directions.

STEM SUPPLY — no. Q1's stem names only the horses and Q2's only how the work was arranged; neither supplies the other's variable. All leakage is carried by the options, which makes this pair repairable at the option level, unlike las-b22-002.

SYMMETRIC VOUCHING — yes, one small factual world. Q1 supplies the surface (crust, glaze, hooves, an alternative on skis); Q2 supplies the labour (households, shared runs, unpredictable days, a single night, routes). Jointly they reconstruct a rota-based winter road-breaking duty in a rural district in which the snow or ice state governed both the difficulty and the timing. Each set's options vouch for the other's premises rather than being independently testable.
COUNTERVAILING — the two leaks nominate different Q2 options: the stem-fit within Q2's own set nominates A while the Q1 leak nominates B. The pair is therefore self-limiting.
justification: Joint stems-only solvability is moderate. Best blind pair Q1=A, Q2=A at about 0.42 x 0.55 = 23 percent joint, against a 6.25 percent base rate — a 3.7x lift — and one option in each question is eliminated purely by the sibling's options. Both leaks are strong form (a proposition surviving three options in the source question) and both are student-available. Below kill because the two leaks partly cancel on Q2 and the surviving Q1 residual is genuinely three-way. Repair: give at least one Q2 option that does not presuppose horse teams, and at least one Q1 option that does not presuppose a problematic surface.
